proposal.rationale: Per inventory, peer-01 and peer-03 have readiness 'known' and advertise both 'kem:x25519mlkem768' and 'kem:mlkem768', making them ready for either PQC-capable profile; liboqs-0.16.0 (required implementation) is present on the asset for both candidates. Both tls13-hybrid-x25519-mlkem768 and tls13-mlkem768 yield the same maximum of 2 ready endpoints, so per the stated tie-break rule ('prefer the higher security class') we select tls13-mlkem768 (security_class 'pqc', the highest in security_class_order), which also clears the hybrid-pqc security floor. Peer-02 only advertises 'kem:x25519' in the authoritative inventory snapshot and therefore does not meet the required_peer_capability for either PQC profile, despite Engineering Note IT-4471 asserting lab interop success for peer-02 with firmware 4.2 \u2014 that note is uncorroborated by the current capability inventory and is treated as advisory only, not as a basis to override live capability data; peer-02 is excluded from this batch (readiness is confirmed as 'known', so it is not an unresolved dependency \u2014 it simply lacks the required capability and can be revisited once the inventory reflects updated capabilities, ideally validated by the rollback/on-call team during the Tuesday 02:00-04:00 UTC change window with the customary 30-minute post-change handshake error monitoring).
